Please send a revised draft reflecting the above, or let us know if you would prefer to discuss.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for your comments. Attached is Seller’s revised draft reflecting movement on several points.

Seller is prepared to move from its initial price and has proposed USD 43,000,000, with a customary adjustment mechanism for cash, debt, unpaid transaction expenses, and normalized working capital to be agreed. We have also revised the closing timing to a 45-day outside date, subject to customary approvals and closing conditions. Seller is comfortable with confirmatory diligence proceeding promptly, but does not agree to an open-ended diligence condition or a broad MAE walk-right beyond the customary formulation reflected in the draft.

We have expanded the representations, covenants, closing deliverables, conditions, survival, and indemnity provisions to address the categories identified in your note. The financial statement representation has also been revised, though Seller has retained appropriate materiality and GAAP-consistency concepts consistent with a private-company transaction of this nature. The confidentiality provision now includes customary disclosure carve-outs.

Please let us know if Buyer would like to discuss the remaining economic and risk-allocation points this week.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. Subject to adjustment as set forth in this Agreement, the Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 43,000,000 for the Shares at Closing. The Purchase Price shall be adjusted on a dollar-for-dollar basis for the Company's cash, indebtedness, unpaid transaction expenses, and the amount, if any, by which normalized working capital as of Closing is greater or less than the mutually agreed target working capital, in each case determined in accordance with the Company's historical accounting practices consistently applied.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur no later than 45 days after signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions precedent set forth in this Agreement, including receipt of required governmental or third-party approvals, delivery of customary closing deliverables, and the absence of any Material Adverse Effect. Buyer shall be entitled to complete confirmatory diligence prior to Closing solely with respect to matters identified in writing within 10 business days after signing and not otherwise disclosed to Buyer before signing.

3. Representations. The Seller represents and warrants to Buyer that: (a) Seller has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of liens other than restrictions arising under securities laws or this Agreement; (b) Seller has the requisite power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (c) the execution and performance of this Agreement by Seller do not conflict with Seller's organizational documents or any material contract binding on Seller; (d) the Company is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing in its jurisdiction of organization; (e) the capitalization of the Company is as set forth in the disclosure schedules; and (f) the financial statements delivered to Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated, in accordance with the accounting principles historically used by the Company, consistently applied, subject to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes in the case of unaudited financial statements.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and all non-public information exchanged in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby are confidential and shall not be disclosed by either party except to its affiliates, representatives, financing sources, insurers, auditors, tax advisers, legal counsel, regulators, or as required by applicable law, regulation, legal process, or stock exchange rule; provided that any recipient of such information is informed of its confidential nature or is otherwise bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties of confidentiality.

5. Additional Seller and Company Representations. Except as set forth in the disclosure schedules, Seller represents and warrants that: (a) the Company has no material undisclosed liabilities except liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business since the date of the latest balance sheet; (b) the Company has filed all material tax returns required to be filed and paid all material taxes due; (c) the Company is in material compliance with applicable laws; (d) the material contracts listed in the disclosure schedules are in full force and effect and, to Seller's knowledge, no material default exists thereunder; (e) there is no pending, or to Seller's knowledge threatened, material litigation against the Company; (f) the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment and benefits laws; (g) to Seller's knowledge, the Company owns or has sufficient rights to use the intellectual property material to the operation of the business; (h) to Seller's knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable data privacy and cybersecurity laws; and (i) no broker, finder, or investment banker is entitled to any fee from Buyer or the Company in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby based on arrangements made by Seller.

6. Interim Operating Covenants. From signing until Closing, except as consented to by Buyer, required by law, contemplated by this Agreement, or set forth in the disclosure schedules, Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course of business in all material respects and to use commercially reasonable efforts to preserve its material business relationships. Buyer shall not unreasonably withhold, condition, or delay any requested consent.

7. Conditions Precedent. Buyer's obligation to close shall be subject to: (a) the Seller fundamental representations being true and correct in all material respects; (b) the other Seller and Company representations being true and correct except where the failure to be true and correct would not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect; (c) Seller's material compliance with pre-closing covenants; (d) receipt of required approvals; and (e) delivery of customary transfer instruments and officer certificates. Seller's obligation to close shall be subject to Buyer's representations being true and correct in all material respects, Buyer's material compliance with its covenants, and Buyer's delivery of the Purchase Price.

8. Indemnification; Survival. The fundamental representations shall survive for 36 months following Closing, tax representations shall survive until 60 days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations, and all other representations shall survive for 12 months following Closing. Seller's aggregate liability for non-fundamental representation claims shall be subject to a deductible equal to 1% of the Purchase Price and capped at 10% of the Purchase Price. Seller's aggregate liability for all claims other than fraud shall not exceed the Purchase Price. Neither party shall be liable for punitive, exemplary, or consequential damages except to the extent awarded to a third party.

9. Closing Deliverables. At Closing, Seller shall deliver customary instruments of transfer for the Shares, officer certificates, resignations of directors or officers requested by Buyer at least five business days before Closing, and other customary documents reasonably necessary to consummate the transfer of the Shares. Buyer shall deliver the Purchase Price and evidence of authority to consummate the transaction.

receiver.private_reasoning: Seller has moved from USD 45.0mm to USD 43.0mm and added a price adjustment, but the revised draft still leaves several buyer-side protections underdeveloped or overly seller-favorable. There is no inadvertently disclosed confidential information in comments/metadata/hidden text; only ordinary document properties. For negotiation, Buyer should not accept USD 43.0mm. A credible counter at USD 40.5mm, with a willingness to discuss movement if Seller provides stronger diligence access and risk allocation, preserves leverage. The working-capital mechanism also needs specificity and should not simply default to the Company’s historical practices if those are not GAAP-consistent. Closing/diligence language is too restrictive: Buyer needs access to confirmatory diligence and a condition tied to no materially adverse findings, at least for identified diligence categories. Financial statements rep should be GAAP-compliant or otherwise tightly scheduled. Indemnity/survival provisions are referenced in the cover note but not visible in the provided excerpt, so Buyer should ask for complete draft provisions or markups.

receiver.requested_changes: Buyer requests the following revisions: (1) reduce the headline purchase price to USD 40,500,000, subject to the agreed adjustment mechanism; (2) specify a detailed closing statement process, target working capital amount, dispute procedure, and accounting hierarchy, with GAAP prevailing over inconsistent historical practices; (3) broaden Buyer’s confirmatory diligence access and make closing conditional on no material adverse findings in agreed diligence categories; (4) revise the MAE and closing condition language to preserve customary Buyer protections; (5) strengthen the financial-statement representation to require GAAP compliance, except as specifically disclosed; (6) provide the full revised draft provisions for survival, indemnity, caps, baskets, escrow/holdback, covenants, disclosure schedules, and closing deliverables; and (7) clarify that required resignations and closing deliverables will be delivered without artificial timing constraints where reasonably requested by Buyer.
receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for Seller’s revised draft. Buyer appreciates Seller’s movement and the addition of a purchase-price adjustment mechanism and expanded transaction provisions. We have reviewed the revised draft and remain prepared to proceed constructively, but several economic and risk-allocation points remain open.

On price, Buyer is not prepared to proceed at USD 43,000,000. Based on the current diligence record, the remaining confirmatory diligence items, and the risk profile reflected in Seller’s proposed limitations, Buyer would be prepared to move forward at USD 40,500,000, subject to a customary cash-free/debt-free adjustment for cash, indebtedness, unpaid transaction expenses, and normalized working capital.

We also need the adjustment mechanism to be more fully specified. The draft should include the target working capital amount, a closing statement delivery and review process, an independent accountant dispute mechanism, and an accounting hierarchy under which GAAP applies except to the extent specific, mutually agreed historical practices are set forth in an exhibit. Buyer cannot accept an open-ended reference to historical practices where those practices have not been identified and tested.

On diligence and closing conditions, Seller’s proposed language is too narrow. Buyer can agree that confirmatory diligence should proceed promptly and not be open-ended, but Buyer needs reasonable access through closing and a condition that no material adverse findings arise in the principal diligence areas identified by Buyer, including financial statements, tax, material contracts, indebtedness, litigation, employment, compliance, and customer/vendor matters. We can discuss a focused list to avoid uncertainty, but the current formulation—limited only to matters identified within 10 business days after signing and not otherwise disclosed—is not sufficient.

The financial-statement representation also requires further revision. Buyer requests that the representation state that the financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company in accordance with GAAP consistently applied, subject only to normal year-end adjustments and absence of footnotes for unaudited statements, and except as specifically set forth on the disclosure schedules.

Finally, your cover note indicates revisions to survival, indemnity, covenants, closing conditions, and related provisions, but the excerpt we have does not permit us to evaluate the full package. Please circulate the complete revised draft, including the proposed survival periods, baskets, caps, exclusions, escrow or holdback mechanics, special indemnities, covenants, disclosure schedules, and closing deliverables. Buyer will need an indemnity package commensurate with the diligence limitations and the private-company nature of the transaction.

Subject to the above, Buyer is available this week to discuss economics and the risk-allocation package. We believe the parties should be able to bridge the remaining issues if Seller can move on price and provide customary Buyer protections.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
